title: How Duke wrote for individuals and built records in the studio
summary: Duke gave each player parts that fit them, and record numbers grew from a theme and solos.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I mean, that was also Duke's concept, wasn't it?
Yeah.
Because he was doing the same kind of thing on piano. He was also -- when he'd come in, he'd work in melody, he'd work melody into things, wouldn't he? He'd contribute melody to the number as well.
Well, he would -- all the time, he would give certain things to different people for what he would want.
Yeah.
He was very shrewd in that. You know. He wrote a song or something, he would give it to the person which idea that he had.
Yeah.
And what he wanted. And it always was successful, because he wrote for these different type of people.

Well, Cootie, when that was happening like that, when it was being built in the record session, which it was so often, you know. I mean, I remember those things getting themselves created as they were happening, you know. In that case, very often he didn't have a -- well, maybe he had an eight bar theme, but not more.
Yeah.

He had a theme, or maybe it was somebody's theme. Maybe it wasn't even his. But there was a theme there. But then, as he would point to you or call on you or call on Johnny or somebody, he was looking for something else to come out of it.
Yes.
For it to be built on from there.
Right.
In another color, in another sound or another feel, or maybe a progression right from what it originally was. But this is how it got itself built, isn't it?
Right.
Well, the person that -- I mean if he'd turn around and call on you, in that instance, you are working from chords.
But I have heard some type of melody.
Yeah. You know how it started out.
Yeah.
So you know what vein you're in.
Yeah.
Yeah. Right. Mostly those things were 32 bars, weren't they?
Yeah.
Because they were three minute records. So --

But I think in chord construction, the idea came in later years. The chord construction thing, for people to play on the chord. That came in later years. But in our generation, I think it was the melody. And you played off the melody, with the chord construction. But you had a foundation there of melody. Something to go by.
Yeah.
Other than the chords.
